title: Hearsay or Fact? How Framing and Elicitation Shape LLM Probability Updates
abstract: arXiv:2610.27745v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judgment assistants and as stand-in participants in psychology experiments, yet little is known about how much their probability estimates move in response to a single new piece of information. We pair premise-hypothesis items from $\delta$-SNLI with one strengthener and one weakener each, elicit the prior and the posteriors in separate calls, and measure the directional movement s: the mean posterior change signed by the annotated direction, so that the prior cancels out. We vary whether the update is stated ("Here is something else you learned") or reported ("Someone said that"), and whether the model gives one probability or five weighted estimates. translated_title: 道听途说还是事实？框架与引出方式如何塑造大语言模型的概率更新
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）日益被用作判断助手以及心理学实验中的替代被试，然而人们对它们的概率估计在响应单条新信息时会发生多大变化却知之甚少。我们将 δ-SNLI 中的前提-假设条目与一个增强项和一个削弱项分别配对，在分离的调用中分别引出先验概率和后验概率，并测量方向性移动 s：即按标注方向赋以符号的后验平均变化量，从而使先验的影响相互抵消。我们变化了信息更新的呈现方式——是直接告知（“这里还有一些你了解到的东西”）还是传闻转述（“有人说”），以及模型是给出单个概率还是五个加权估计。我们测试了七种配置：两个本地模型（Qwen3-8B、OLMo-2-7B；240 对）和五种通过智能体命令行框架运行的配置（120 对），且假设与分析规则在正式运行前即已固定（不公开……）
tldr: 该论文提出了一种衡量大语言模型对单条新信息概率更新幅度的“方向性移动”指标，并发现信息的框架呈现方式（直接告知还是传闻转述）与概率引出方式（单个概率还是五个加权估计）会显著影响模型的概率更新。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a directional-movement metric to measure how much LLM probability estimates shift in response to a single new piece of information, showing that framing (stated vs. hearsay-reported) and elicitation format (single vs. five weighted estimates) shape the magnitude of LLM probability updates.
